newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cenbank flood credits at 22, 25 pct -source.
newsitem.headline: Polish cenbank flood credits at 22, 25 pct -source.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland's 2.5 billion zloty flood relief credit for the government is divided into two parts, of which one carries interest at 22 percent and the other 25 percent, a senior financial source said.
"A part of the credit is based on T-bill yields and is 22 percent and the other is at the central bank's lombard rate of 25 percent," the source, who asked not to be named, said.
Last week parliament amended this year's budget law to let the government borrow an additional 2.5 billion zlotys of flood relief money from the central bank after the government.

The central bank has said that alhough it would lend the money "at market rates" the credit would come much cheaper for the government than borrowing on the market because the NBP profit from the loan would eventually go back to the budget.
The finance ministry said it has so far borrowed one billion zlotys, but has not spent any of the cash yet.
The two-week deluge, the worst in centuries, inundated more than 5,000 square km killing 55 people, forcing tens of thousands out of their homes and causing widespread damage.
